cohort: 100 obese women (BMI >= 30 kg/m^2) and 100 women with normal BMI (18.5-24.9 kg/m^2)
finding: Obese pregnant women had a significantly higher incidence of gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and pre-eclampsia compared to non-obese pregnant women.
mod_finding: The main indication for primary cesarean section in the obese group was cephalopelvic disproportion (20%).
birth_weight: Majority of newborns in the obese group (58%) had a birth weight between 3-3.9 kg, and macrosomia was seen in 4%.
